- When sentiment is negative in the recent 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to account for bearish momentum.  
- If model forecast spikes sharply (e.g., >10% above recent 10-day average), reduce by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 10-day moving average), adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., 0.00 or ±0.5), avoid large upward revisions; use 1–2% conservative correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently above true outcome by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias of 1–2% per day.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive -1.00), reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast is below true outcome by >2% for 3+ consecutive days, consider upward bias of 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
